title: No vesting at or before the start
summary: Pure model: the vested quantity is zero whenever the reference time is at or before the schedule start.

title: Full vesting at or after the end
summary: Pure model: with start < finish, the vested quantity equals the original total whenever the reference time is at or after the finish.

title: Vested quantities and remainders stay within bounds
summary: Pure model: for a nonnegative total and start < finish, the vested quantity stays between zero and the total, and the required remainder is nonnegative.

title: Vesting is nondecreasing over time
summary: Pure model: for a nonnegative total and start < finish, increasing the reference time cannot decrease the vested quantity.

title: Key-authorized claim acceptance
summary: In constructed single-native-asset contexts, checked cases cover symbolic identities, a nonnegative total, start < now < finish, and sufficient continuation funding, with fixed address/ADA scaffolding. Fixed full-retention cases also cover other reference times. The broader partial-claim target remains unproved.

title: Script-authorized claim acceptance
summary: In the fixed midpoint, single-native-asset context, a zero withdrawal keyed by the symbolic beneficiary script authorizes the claim without a key signature. The continuation retains the full original quantity.

title: Two separately funded continuations are accepted
summary: In the fixed two-identical-input context at time 1500, two continuations holding 50 native tokens each satisfy the claim checked for the first input.

title: Full-claim acceptance after vesting ends
summary: For the fixed native-asset datum and beneficiary signature, a claim at now >= 2000 accepts with any nonnegative continuation token quantity. This theorem still constructs one continuing output.

title: Authorized cancellation after recovery
summary: For the fixed datum and locker key signature, cancellation accepts whenever now > 3000. The constructed context still contains one output.

title: Partial claims preserve the datum and remainder
summary: In the fixed one-input/one-output midpoint context, acceptance forces the arbitrary output datum to match the input. The native-token quantity must be at least 50. The broader native-asset soundness target remains unproved.

title: Accepted cancellation occurs after recovery
summary: For the fixed datum and signed locker key, cancellation acceptance implies now > 3000. This does not derive authorization for arbitrary cancellation contexts.

title: Unauthorized key claims are rejected
summary: The compiled validator rejects claims with a key beneficiary and no signatories in contexts built with mkClaimCtx and withAsset. The fixed midpoint case also rejects a single non-beneficiary signer.

title: Underfunded partial continuations are rejected
summary: In the fixed single-native-asset midpoint context, a continuation holding fewer than 50 tokens causes rejection. The broader native-asset shortfall-rejection target remains unproved.

title: Changed continuation datums are rejected
summary: For valid single-asset schedules before vesting ends, the compiled validator rejects contexts built with mkClaimCtx and withAsset whose output datum differs from the input datum.

title: Hash-datum claim inputs are rejected
summary: In the fixed partial-claim context, replacing the input's inline datum with a symbolic datum hash causes rejection, even though script info still supplies the resolved datum.

title: Script claims without withdrawals are rejected
summary: In the fixed midpoint context with a symbolic script beneficiary, a claim with no withdrawals or key signatures is rejected.

title: Premature cancellation is rejected
summary: For the fixed datum and authorized locker key, cancellation is rejected whenever now <= 3000.

title: Unauthorized cancellation is rejected
summary: For the fixed datum at now > 3000, cancellation without the locker key signature is rejected.

title: One remainder cannot satisfy two fixed inputs
summary: In the fixed two-identical-input midpoint context, a single continuation holding 50 native tokens causes rejection.

title: A merged continuation is rejected
summary: In the fixed two-identical-input midpoint context, a single continuation holding 100 native tokens is rejected despite covering both inputs' aggregate required remainder.

title: Aggregate batch funding does not replace individual funding
summary: In the fixed two-identical-input midpoint context, continuations holding 40 and 60 native tokens are rejected because one falls below its required remainder of 50.
